newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-ministers Pasqua, Madelin fire on Juppe.
newsitem.headline: French ex-ministers Pasqua, Madelin fire on Juppe.

text.p: Former ministers Charles Pasqua and Alain Madelin have both rounded on French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, saying they planned to tell voters across the country of their grievances.
Pasqua, a former hardline interior minister, attended a joint rally with sacked finance minister Madelin in the town of Villandry, south-west of Paris, late on Sunday.

In a thinly-veiled reference to the government's recent campaign to boost voter confidence despite near-record unemployment and poor growth prospects, Pasqua told supporters there was no point in "running after the people's confidence, measure after measure, opinion poll after opinion poll".

"I have decided to speak directly to all those who don't want to jump ship, that is France, because they don't find it as bad as all that," Pasqua said, adding that his presence alongside Madelin marked the launch of a big national debate.
Pasqua is a member of Juppe's Gaullist RPR, while Madelin belongs to the centre-right UDF, junior partner in the ruling coalition.
Madelin spotlighted what he called the huge gap between French leaders and those they represent. "It's clear that today France is depressed, that unemployment is still biting."

Several leading members of the ruling coalition including former prime minister Edouard Balladur and National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin have criticised Juppe in recent days, calling for stimulation of the economy and tax reform.
